title: Strata of a flat constructible sheaf and generation by $a_!L$
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and $X$ a Noetherian scheme (for
instance of finite type over the standing field), on the étale or the
pro-étale site.

1. If $F$ is a flat constructible sheaf of $A$-modules on $X$, there is a
finite partition $X=\bigsqcup_{k=1}^mS_k$ into locally closed subschemes,
ordered so that $X_{\ge k}=\bigcup_{k'\ge k}S_{k'}$ is closed and $S_k$ is open in
$X_{\ge k}$, such that each $F|_{S_k}$ is locally constant with stalks finite
projective $A$-modules.
2. For such a partition, with $a_k:S_k\hookrightarrow X$ the inclusions and
$L_k=F|_{S_k}$, $F$ is an iterated extension of the sheaves $a_{k!}L_k$; each
$a_{k!}L_k$ is flat constructible and lies in $\Dctf(X,A)$.
3. $\Dctf(X,A)$ is the smallest full subcategory of $D(X,A)$ containing the
objects $a_!L$ ($a:S\hookrightarrow X$ locally closed, $L$ locally constant
with finite projective stalks) and closed under shifts, extensions (cones)
and direct summands.

Conventions. On either small site use ordinary sheaves of modules over the constant ring $A$ and their unbounded derived category. Here $\Dctf$ consists of objects with bounded constructible cohomology and Tor amplitude in some finite interval: $H^r(C\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}N[0])=0$ outside the interval for every module sheaf $N$. Flat means that ordinary tensoring with the sheaf is exact; finite projective means a direct summand of a finite free $A$-module. For a locally closed immersion $a$, factor it as the open immersion $j$ into its scheme-theoretic closure followed by the closed immersion $g$ into $X$ and write $a_!=g_*j_!$. The subcategories in clause (3) are understood to be closed under isomorphisms. A partition of the empty scheme may have no strata.

proof.text: The Noetherian hypothesis implies that the underlying space has the descending chain condition on closed subsets. Thus every open subset is quasi-compact: a cover with no finite subcover would give a strictly increasing chain of finite unions of its members, hence a strictly decreasing chain of their closed complements. The same argument on every affine open makes every open immersion below quasi-compact. For a closed immersion into X, its inverse image over an affine chart Spec(B) is Spec(B/I) by the affine-quotient clause of the closed-immersion definition. An ideal of B/I is the image of its inverse-image ideal in B, so generators of the latter give generators of the former. Hence B/I is Noetherian, and the closed subscheme is locally Noetherian; its closed underlying subspace is quasi-compact by the same finite-subcover argument. Apply the locally Noetherian quasi-separatedness lemma to X and to these closed subschemes: they are all qcqs. These facts verify the quasi-compact-complement hypotheses of the pro-etale localization results used below.

source.place: Clause (2): hypotheses of the open-closed induction

proof.text: By the two constructibility definitions choose a finite locally closed partition adapted to F. Refine it, rather than merely reorder its old strata, as follows. For each old stratum T include the two closed sets \overline T and \overline T\setminus T, and let \mathcal Z consist of X, the empty set and all intersections of this finite family. Set S_Z=Z\setminus\bigcup_{Z'\in\mathcal Z,\ Z'\subsetneq Z}Z'. Each point belongs to the cell of the smallest member of \mathcal Z containing it, so these cells partition X; their membership in every old \overline T and its boundary shows that each cell lies in one old T. Order the nonempty cells by any linear order extending reverse inclusion of their Z. Among the Z with nonempty cells, the unprocessed ones form a downward closed family. If x lies in such a Z, the smallest member Z_x containing x is a subset of Z and has the nonempty cell containing x, so its cell is also unprocessed. Thus the union of the unprocessed cells equals the finite union of their Z, hence is closed; this also handles Z whose own cell was empty. Thus every tail is closed and its first cell is open in it. Give each cell the open subscheme structure inside the reduced induced closed subscheme on Z, supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. It maps to its old stratum T: locally where T is closed, its defining ideal is contained in the radical ideal of the reduced cell, since every cell point belongs to T. The affine quotient description therefore factors the cell immersion through T, and these local factorizations agree because immersions are monomorphisms. Pulling the old trivializing covers and constant models back along these actual maps gives finite locally constant restrictions. Each cell is constructible because it is a difference of closed sets in the Noetherian space, by [def-weil-constructible-subset]. This writes out the finite closed-set refinement argument. If X is empty use the empty partition.

source.place: Clause (1): ordered refinement of an adapted partition

proof.text: For either site the geometric-stalk adjunction is a morphism of topoi by [lem-fix-geometric-stalk-topos-point]. Apply the ringed-topos flat-pullback theorem to this point with coefficient ring its stalk A: a flat F has flat geometric stalks. No conservativity of pro-etale geometric points is used. Every finite local module model on a nonempty trivializing object is isomorphic to such a stalk. If M is one of these finite A-modules, choose a finite set of generators and a surjection A^n\to M. Its kernel is a finite set because A^n is finite, hence is generated by finitely many of its elements. This supplies a finite presentation A^r\to A^n\to M\to0. The existing finitely-presented-flat-module theorem makes M finite projective. The same applies directly to every finite geometric stalk. This proves clause (1).

source.place: Clause (1): flat stalks and finite projectivity

proof.text: We first record the sheaf calculation needed for clause (2), on both sites. For a complementary open/closed pair j,i, restriction is exact and commutes with ordinary tensor: on the etale site use the exact module inverse image, and on the pro-etale site use the identified-constant-coefficient operations; the algebraic inverse-image tensor comparison applies to both. The etale open-closed sequence is [lem-weil-pbc-open-closed-short-exact], and its pro-etale counterpart, exact i_*, and all four restriction identities are [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed]. In the etale case the open unit, closed counit, and the two vanishing lemmas give the same identities j^*j_!=1, i^*i_*=1, i^*j_!=0, j^*i_*=0; the maps are module-linear because their underlying adjunction maps are. Exactness of i_* in this case is explicitly part of [lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement]. On either site the open-closed sequence shows that a sheaf with both restrictions zero is zero. For any short exact sequence, tensor with H and form its homology objects (including the outer kernel and cokernel). If j^*H and i^*H are flat, exactness and the tensor comparison imply that each such homology object restricts to zero on both sides, hence is zero. Thus tensor with H preserves short exact sequences: flatness can be tested on this open/closed pair. In particular j_! and i_* preserve flat sheaves, using their restriction identities. This argument works for all module sheaves, including nonclassical pro-etale test sheaves. We also need to compare scheme structures, rather than identify a topologically open immersion with an open immersion of schemes. If h:T→Y is a surjective closed immersion, its open complement is empty. The same sequences give an isomorphism of the unit H→h_*h^*H, and the closed counit gives h^*h_*≅1. Thus h^* and h_* are inverse equivalences for ordinary module sheaves, and a constant A-module sheaf pulls back to the same constant model. Finite local constancy is reflected by h^*: on the etale site h is a universal homeomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-closed-immersion-universal-homeomorphism], so [prop-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-topos] identifies the topoi, constants and covering epimorphisms. On the pro-etale site, apply [new-lem-weil-pbc-proetale-surjective-closed-cover-refinement] to a trivializing cover of T. It gives a cover B of Y whose pullback B×_Y T refines that cover. On each B, the unit and counit just proved for the surjective closed immersion B×_Y T→B identify H|_B with the constant module model on B, since their pullbacks are isomorphic. This proves reflection with the same finite projective models; the empty complement is quasi-compact even when B is not Noetherian.

For a locally constant L with finite projective geometric stalks, each constant model on a nonempty trivializing object is isomorphic to a geometric stalk: choose a geometric point of that object and apply [lem-fix-geometric-stalk-topos-point]. Thus its models are finite projective (empty objects can be discarded). Such L is flat: on a trivializing covering, a displayed splitting M\oplus N=A^r gives L\oplus\underline N=A_S^r, so tensoring any short exact sequence with L is a retract of its r-fold direct sum, which is short exact. Exactness can be checked on the covering: kernels and cokernels restrict to zero, hence vanish by the sheaf axiom and local lifting of sections. Factor a:S\hookrightarrow X as an open j:S\hookrightarrow\overline S followed by a closed g:\overline S\hookrightarrow X, and put a_!=g_*j_!. Step 4 makes a_!L flat. Its restrictions are L on S and zero on \overline S\setminus S and X\setminus\overline S, by the same restriction identities. These three pieces are locally closed and hence constructible in the Noetherian space by [def-weil-constructible-subset], so a_!L is constructible on either site by the constructibility definitions. Finally a_!L[0] is a bounded-above complex of flat sheaves, hence K-flat by [lem-weil-pbc-independent-bounded-flat-kflat]. Its derived tensor with every module sheaf N[0] is the degree-zero ordinary tensor a_!L\otimes_A N. It therefore has Tor amplitude [0,0] and belongs to \Dctf. This proves the assertion about all generators, not only the strata of one F.

source.place: Clause (2): flat constructible extension by zero and Tor amplitude zero

proof.text:
First verify closed/open interchange on either site. In a cartesian square with closed g:Z→X, open u:W→X, open v:Z_W→Z and closed h:Z_W→W, the restriction formula for direct image gives u^*g_*v_!L≅h_*L, so open adjunction gives a map u_!h_*L→g_*v_!L. Pulling back by g, the open-extension base-change statements [lem-cbc-extension-zero-base-change] and [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change] identify the left side with v_!h^*h_*L≅v_!L; the right side is v_!L by the closed counit. The induced map is v_! of that counit and is invertible. On the open complement of Z, the right side is zero; base change for u_! identifies the left side with extension of the restriction of h_*L to W\Z, which is zero by the open/closed vanishing identity. The exact open-closed sequence detects isomorphisms, so the map is an isomorphism. Every complement here is quasi-compact by step 1. This also identifies the definition g_*j_! using scheme-theoretic closure with u_!h_* in any open W where the immersion is closed: the closure restricted to W is that closed subscheme, since its affine defining kernel is the same quotient ideal.
Induct on the number of ordered strata, allowing the given strata to have arbitrary locally closed subscheme structures. With no strata the open-closed sequence for the empty closed/open pair gives F=0 and the extension tower is empty. Otherwise let U be the actual open subscheme of X with underlying set S_1, and let i:C→X be the reduced induced closed subscheme on its complement, using [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Write u:U→X for the open immersion. The immersion S_1→X factors as a surjective closed immersion h:S_1→U followed by u: in a closed-then-open factorization, the latter open contains U and the defining ideal restricts to U. Step 4 gives F|_U≅h_*L_1. The open-closed sequence is therefore 0→u_!h_*L_1→F→i_*i^*F→0. Here u_!h_*L_1≅a_{1!}L_1 by the closed/open calculation just proved.
For k≥2 use D_k=S_k×_X C with maps b_k:D_k→C and p_k:D_k→S_k. Base change preserves immersions by [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft]; p_k is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] and is surjective because C has precisely the closed underlying tail, and a closed immersion has unchanged residue fields, so the fibre over any point of S_k in the tail is that same point ([lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-points]). The D_k give the remaining ordered partition of C. The sheaf i^*F is flat by flat pullback and constructible: its restriction to D_k is p_k^*L_k, with the pulled-back local trivializations. Apply the induction hypothesis on C, which is Noetherian by step 1. Exact i_* gives a tower with factors i_*b_{k!}p_k^*L_k.
These factors equal a_{k!}L_k as follows. Use the closed/open calculation to compute extension along an immersion in an open neighbourhood W in which its image is closed. The intersection D_k→X has the same locally closed underlying image as S_k. In such a W the two immersions are closed and the map D_k→S_k is the surjective closed immersion p_k. Step 4 identifies L_k≅p_{k*}p_k^*L_k. Closed direct images compose, since their values on V are sections on V×_W D_k. Extending the resulting isomorphism by zero from W proves i_*b_{k!}p_k^*L_k≅a_{k!}L_k; computing the left side inside C first agrees by closed/open interchange for C→X and W→X, followed by composition of the closed direct images. Thus the first sequence and the pushed-forward tower prove clause (2), including nonreduced strata, without assuming that S_1→X itself is open.

source.place: Clause (2): induction on the ordered finite partition

proof.text: The category \Dctf is thick. On the etale site, bounded constructible complexes are triangulated by [prop-constructible-derived-subcategory]. They are also closed under retracts: if e is the idempotent on each constructible cohomology sheaf induced by a retract, its image is the kernel of 1-e and is constructible by [thm-constructible-serre]; the same finite cohomological bounds persist. Tensoring a triangle with any N[0] is triangulated by [lem-kun-derived-tensor-triangulated], so its cohomology long exact sequence shows that an extension of objects with intervals [a,b] and [c,d] has interval [min(a,c),max(b,d)]. A shift by n replaces [a,b] by [a-n,b-n], and a retract retains the interval because its tensor cohomology is a retract of the original tensor cohomology. These arguments prove the etale assertion. For the pro-etale site use the exact comparison and its triangulated derived functor, the equivalence of bounded constructible categories [sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison], and the interval-preserving equivalence [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian]. Here X is qcqs by step 1 and A is Noetherian since its finite set of ideals has no infinite increasing chain. This transfer respects ambient cones: lift the connecting morphism between the two bounded constructible ends by full faithfulness and take its etale cone. It respects ambient retracts too: on each cohomology sheaf lift the associated idempotent by the sheaf equivalence, take its etale image as above, and apply exact comparison. Thus the other cone or retract stays bounded constructible before applying the Tor comparison. All these are ordinary constant-ring module categories.

source.place: Clause (3): the finite-Tor constructible subcategory is thick

proof.text: Let C\in\Dctf(X,A), with Tor interval [a,b], a\le b. On the etale site [lem-sf-etale-flat-constructible] gives an isomorphic complex P, zero outside [a,b], whose terms are flat constructible. On the pro-etale site first use [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian] to choose C_0\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\mathrm{et}},A) with \nu_X^*C_0\cong C and the same interval. Apply the same etale model theorem to C_0 and pull its model back termwise. The comparison functor is exact and commutes with cohomology, so the pulled-back complex represents C and remains zero outside [a,b]. Its terms are constructible by the sheaf equivalence and flat by the ringed-topos flat-pullback theorem. Hence a bounded flat constructible model exists on either site for the general finite ring and general Noetherian X of this item. This cites the independent model theorem, not the parent sk-lem-sf-flat-model which uses this item.

source.place: Clause (3): constructible flat models, without the circular parent citation

proof.text: Let \mathcal G be the full replete subcategory generated by the a_!L under the three indicated operations. By steps 5 and 7, \mathcal G\subseteq\Dctf. For the reverse inclusion use P from step 8. Write P_{\ge q} for its brutal tail, with P^r in degrees r\ge q and zero below. Inclusion of the next tail and projection onto degree q give a degreewise split short exact sequence 0\to P_{\ge q+1}\to P_{\ge q}\to P^q[-q]\to0: in degree q it is 0\to0\to P^q\xrightarrow{1}P^q\to0, above q it is 0\to P^r\xrightarrow{1}P^r\to0\to0, and below q every term is zero. The complex maps commute with differentials since the tail differential only points upwards and the target single complex has zero differential. The short-exact-sequence triangle theorem supplies a distinguished triangle with these three terms. By steps 3 and 6 each flat constructible P^q is a finite extension of a_!L; placing its short exact sequences in degree zero and applying the same triangle theorem gives P^q[0]\in\mathcal G, hence P^q[-q]\in\mathcal G. Start with P_{\ge b+1}=0 (a cone of an identity of a generator) and induct down from b to a along these triangles. This gives P_{\ge a}=P\in\mathcal G, so C\in\mathcal G. This proves clause (3).

lean.note: All three clauses are stated separately for both sites. Dctf is expanded as bounded constructible cohomology and the recorded finite Tor-amplitude condition, as the node conventions specify.
